releases.name: 2.0.1 — Workspace Resolution Fix
releases.body:
## EchoesVault 2.0.1 — Workspace Resolution Fix
Fixed an issue where globally installed OpenCode plugins could incorrectly select / as the EchoesVault workspace.
- Prioritizes the active project directory
- Uses the reported worktree only as a fallback
- Prevents all writes to filesystem roots
- Adds regression coverage for global plugin environments

releases.name: 2.0.0 - Shared Memory Across Codex and OpenCode
releases.body:
## EchoesVault for OpenCode 2.0.0
Major update introducing EchoesVault Protocol 1.0.0 compatibility.
- Shared repository-local runtime with Codex and other agents
- Conflict-safe daily logs and deterministic index generation
- Atomic writes and SHA-256 protection for page updates
- Unified local state and improved TUI status
- Explicit, safe migration from OpenCode 1.x
- No repository changes during plugin installation
After updating, run /echoes-init once in existing repositories to migrate them. Python 3.9+ is required.

releases.name: 1.2.3 - User-Controlled Vault Status
releases.body:
- EchoesVault status transitions now require explicit user commands.
- Memory Saved is set only after /echoes-end.
- /echoes-init and /echoes-start are likewise protected from autonomous agent calls.
- Removed automatic session-status resets when OpenCode starts.
- Updated sidebar messaging and documentation to clarify the workflow.

# Release v1.2.2: Prompt Architecture & Maintainability 🚀

This release focuses on significantly improving how the AI interacts with the Vault, hardening the system rules, and making the codebase much easier to maintain for future updates and contributors.

## ✨ Features & Prompt Improvements
* **Hardened System Rules:** The AI instructions for `/echoes-init`, `/echoes-resume`, and `/echoes-end` have been completely rewritten to enforce strict "Read-Before-Write" behavior and prevent context hallucination.
* **Obsidian Dataview Support:** The AI is now strictly instructed to include YAML frontmatter (with `type`, `stack`, and `status` tags) on all new pages, making the vault fully compatible with advanced Obsidian plugins.
* **Technical Density (ADR):** Improved the "distill and save" logic. The agent is now laser-focused on writing dry, dense Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) rather than verbose chat summaries.
* **Local Assets Awareness:** Added rules for the agent to properly reference local diagrams and schematics from the `assets/` directory.

## 🛠 Refactoring & Under the Hood
* **Extracted System Prompts:** Moved the core AI prompt templates out of the main plugin logic and into dedicated files. This declutters the codebase and makes it significantly easier to tweak, version-control, and test agent instructions.

## 📚 Documentation & Community
* **Updated README:** Added a new **Support the project** section outlining how users can help sustain the development through GitHub Sponsors or by using the OpenCode GO referral link.
* **Polished formatting:** General cleanup of the documentation structure for better readability.

---
**Thank you for using EchoesVault!** If you enjoy this update, please consider dropping a 🌟 on the repository or checking out the new Support section in the README.

## What's new in v1.2.0 ### Vault Health monitor in sidebar The TUI sidebar now shows a live **Vault Health** section (visible after `/echoes-init`): - Colored status bullet — green below 170 pages, yellow at 170–200, red above 200 - **Pages** — current page count in `EchoesVault/pages/` - **Usage** — percentage of the 200-page soft limit (can exceed 100%) - **Consider migrating to RAG** — shown automatically when pages exceed 200 Stats update in real time: at plugin startup and after every vault-modifying operation (`commit_memory`, `append_to_daily_log`, `create_or_update_page`, `activate_vault`). ### Bug fix: TUI failed to load after install Added `@opentui/solid` and `solid-js` as explicit dependencies. Previously the TUI crashed on install with `Cannot find module '@opentui/solid/jsx-dev-runtime'` because these packages were not bundled with the plugin. ### Docs Added **Updating** section to README with the correct force-update command. ### How to update run `opencode plugin echoes-vault-opencode@1.2.0 --force`
